[TALE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.07382) models elapsed-time-dependent item correlations through single-target augmentation, interval weighting and trend-aware normalization. Positional decay measures intervening interactions; elapsed-time decay measures calendar distance—distinct signals for irregular histories. [TSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531) explicitly models repeat consumption using user/item repeat intervals and similarity to previous repeat sequences. Its direct repeat-item mechanism does not transfer cleanly to unseen-item recommendation. A proposed adaptation, rather than a published TALE/TSRec formula: represent recurring interests through h = Σₜ wₜe(iₜ)/Σₜwₜ, with wₜ = exp[−α(L−t)−β log(1+Δt/τ)]. Score unseen candidates by SASRec_score(j)+λhᵀe(j). Repeated similar interests reinforce one another; mask previously consumed items. Ablate positional-only, elapsed-time-only and combined weighting. Compute Δt relative to the latest observed interaction, avoiding future timestamps.

Keep all four categories, fixed users/candidates and prescribed seeds. Compare paired per-user hit indicators; bootstrap users independently within each category, preserving model pairing, then average the four category differences. Report the macro HR@10 difference and a 95% bootstrap interval, conditional on these candidates and trained models; bootstrap intervals have support in [retrieval evaluation research](https://www.nist.gov/publications/computing-confidence-intervals-common-ir-measures). One changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Use a small prespecified ablation grid: repeated validation selection can overfit finite samples ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)); bootstrapping the selected winner does not remove that bias. Preserve the official sampled metric, but avoid inferring full-catalog gains: sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).
